new_findings.title: Usage counts accept values beyond JavaScript safe integer precision
new_findings.defect: Number.isInteger accepts integers that JavaScript cannot represent exactly, so the parser can certify a rounded count as authoritative.
new_findings.failure_scenario: A JSON usage response contains used: 9007199254740993; JSON parsing rounds it to 9007199254740992, which passes Number.isInteger and is rendered as the reported count.
new_findings.fix: Require Number.isSafeInteger for count fields and reject values outside the safe range.

new_findings.title: Streamed response buffering has no byte ceiling
new_findings.defect: The total deadline bounds elapsed time but chunks and total have no response-size limit; the completed body is also copied into a new ArrayBuffer.
new_findings.failure_scenario: An authenticated portal endpoint streams a very large JSON response quickly enough to exceed browser memory before the deadline; the chunk list grows without a cap and the subsequent full-body copy can exhaust the tab or browser.
new_findings.fix: Enforce a maximum accumulated byte count, cancel the reader and reject once exceeded, and cover an over-limit streamed body in a test.

summary: Four corrections hold and APP1-KEYS-RV06 is partial because calendar-invalid timestamps can normalize to valid dates. Two medium findings remain: unsafe usage count precision and uncapped response buffering. The required Python check passed; Vitest and typecheck were not run per the lane brief.
